text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria will receive up to 15 billion cubic metres of natural gas from Russia in the next 15 years at $99.99 per 1,000 cubic metres under a draft bilateral agreement, state owned Bulgargas executive director Vasil Filipov said.

-- Bulgaria's Interior ministry said three former executive directors of state owned Mineralbank, which was declared insolvent at the end of March were detained on charges of misappropriation of funds.
-- The United States and five European countries had supported Bulgaria's willingness for a NATO membership at a meeting in Brussels, the Defence minstry said.
-- Bulgaria is expected to submit on Saturday an aplication for membership in the Central European Free Trade Association, Trade minister Daniela Bobeva said.
-- Bulgaria may import 100,000 tonnes of maize from Croatia to compensate partly an expected shortage of 300,000 tonnes of fodder grain until the new crop, Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said.

-- Bulgaria's First Private Bank (FPB), in receivership since May 17, 1996 now has 1.4 billion levs paid-in capital, which meets central bank requirements for a domestic banking licence, a FPB official said.
-- Bulgaria needs a structure similar to the US Federal Bureau of Investigation to fight organised crime more efficiently, Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces leader Ivan Kostov said.
-- Foreign investments in Bulgaria in the first quarter of 1997 were estimated at $45.2 million after $302.5 million last year, the Agency for Foreign Investments said.

-- The Bulgarian State Railways (BSR) decided to raise passenger fares by 58 percent from April 20 in line with the country's pledges to the International Monetary Fund, BSR executive director Yordan Mirchev said.
-- Bulgaria's Foreign Minister Stoyan Stalev is expected to visit Greece April 14-16 to discuss a possible relaxation of visa requirements for Bulgarians.

-- Bulgaria hopes to sell 30 major state plants in line with pledges to the International Monetary Fund to have 25 percent of private property in the country's economy by June 1, the chairman of the Privatisation Agency's Supervisory board Yossif Iliev said.
